question: A single bench section at a school event can hold either \(7\) adults or \(11\) children. When \(N\) bench sections are connected end to end, an equal number of adults and children seated together will occupy all the bench space. What is the least possible positive integer value of \(N?\)
solution:
One adult uses \(\frac17\) of a section, and one child uses \(\frac1{11}\), so equal numbers of adults and children give a useful equation for the total space.

Let \(P\) be the number of adults and also the number of children. Measuring length in bench sections gives
\[
N=\frac{P}{7}+\frac{P}{11}=\frac{18P}{77}.
\]
Both \(N\) and \(P\) must be positive integers. Since \(77=7\cdot11\) and neither prime divides \(18\), both \(7\) and \(11\) must divide \(P\). Thus \(P\) must be a positive multiple of \(77\).

The smallest possibility is \(P=77\). These adults occupy \(77/7=11\) sections, while the children occupy \(77/11=7\) sections. Therefore the least possible value is
\[
\boxed{N=11+7=18},
\]
which is choice \(\textbf{B}\).
